item.title: Why are we doing this?
item.description:
Why are we doing this? #

One page, before any terminal.

You can now build real software by describing it — what people call vibe coding: you say what you want, a model writes it, you steer. It works, startlingly well. And it has a failure mode everyone who tries it eventually hits: three weeks in, neither you nor the model remembers why anything is the way it is. The code is there; the reasoning evaporated with the chat window it happened in.

item.title: Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools
item.description:
Chapter 2 — Setting up your tools #

This is the macOS course path: written for CIS 7000-008, where every walker has an Anthropic account with Claude Code access (Claude Code is not on the free plan — outside readers, check that first). Hardware: an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) on macOS 15+ — Apple menu → About This Mac to check; Homebrew dropped Intel Macs in 2026, and the Intel fallback is in the Homebrew step. The grey word after each step’s title is its step ID — quote it when you report a mismatch. Windows notes are partial orientation, not a tested walkthrough — corrections genuinely wanted ( open an issue with the step ID). Budget ~40 minutes of steps; installs, logins, and any debugging are extra. The chapter opens by installing the helper — so every later step has someone to ask.

item.title: Chapter 3 — Your first project
item.description:
Chapter 3 — Your first project #

A real project: a Wordle variant, live on GitHub Pages, built with a model collaborator — and your first decisions on the record. The required steps total ~65 minutes of active work (installs, logins, and debugging are extra); each step shows its own estimate, and your actual times are something we genuinely want to hear about. One path; each step says how to verify it worked.

item.title: Tell us what happened
item.description:
Tell us what happened #

A few minutes, two moves — and if you’re reading this page because you’re stopping partway, that’s exactly as valuable: tell us where and why (ten seconds, three boxes), and thank you — the walkers who stop are the ones a guide learns the most from.

The debrief — a record, like everything else ~5 min debrief

☰

Builds on: Your first answers

item.title: Your variables
item.description:
Your variables #

This guide personalizes itself. Two values, entered once, appear in every command that needs them — so what you copy-paste is already yours, not a template you have to patch by hand.

Where they live: in your browser’s local storage, and nowhere else. They never leave your machine, we never see them, and clearing your browser data clears them (the guide then just shows the placeholders again). You can change them here any time and every page updates.
